title: Add invocation phase snapshotter and alert runbook
author: Maya Henderson
description: Context: Long-tail latency/cost incidents frequently require manual stitching across token-level metrics, traces, and dashboard panels. This PR implements a lightweight 'phase snapshotter' that captures per-invocation phase boundaries (tokenize -> encode -> KV-lookup -> kernel-exec -> post-process) and emits a compact snapshot attached to sampled traces. Motivation: give on-call and SREs a fast, queryable artifact for triage that links phase-level durations to token-cost buckets and kernel queue metrics. What this PR does (single continuous description): Adds a Phase Snapshotter service that annotates opentelemetry traces with a single JSON snapshot per sampled invocation. Snapshots contain phase names, start+duration (ms), token-count, model-hash, hw-snapshot tags (GPU type, queue depth). Adds an enrichment hook into the tracing pipeline that synthesizes phase boundaries from existing span timing when direct instrumentation is missing. Adds two Grafana dashboard panels (phase-timeline-sparklines, phase-cohort-slicer) plus an alert playbook (alert-runbook.md) with tuned thresholds and escalation steps. Introduces a small sampling policy tweak: when a token-cost spike is detected we raise trace sampling probability for the next 5 minutes for that tenant. Includes unit and integration tests for snapshot serialization and a lightweight replay helper to attach snapshots to synthetic traces for debugging. Checklist: [x] phase snapshot schema and serializer; [x] tracing enrichment hook; [x] dashboard JSON; [x] alert runbook and playbook links; [x] tests + CI; [x] docs update (observability runbook). Related: ENG-4821 (observability backlog), SUP-889 (customer incident reproducer).

review_comments: Liam O'Connor: Nice work — can you call out the expected cardinality impact of adding snapshots to sampled traces?
